facts.statement: Micropristis lived in the Middle East and Europe during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Micropristis is an extinct genus of ganopristid sclerorhynchoid that lived in the Middle East and Europe during the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Micropristis comes from Cenomanian rocks in Lebanon, while other specimens are found in Santonian-Campanian rocks of Europe.
facts.quote: The type specimen is known from the Cenomanian of Lebanon, and other specimens referrable to this genus have been found in Santonian-Campanian age rocks of Europe.

facts.statement: Micropristis is classified in the order Rajiformes.
Micropristis belongs to the family Rhinobatidae.
Micropristis is a member of the family Sclerorhynchidae.
Micropristis was named by the French paleontologist Henri Cappetta in 1980.
facts.quote: Fue nombrado por el francés Henri Cappetta (1980), un intiólogo especializado en paleontología.

facts.statement: Micropristis has teeth similar to those of Ptychotrygon and possesses facial spines that distinguish it from other fish.
facts.quote: Los dientes de estos peces se asemejan en gran manera a los de la especie Ptychotrygon; además, presentan espinas en sus rostros que los diferencian de otros peces.

facts.statement: Micropristis lived between 100.5 and 89.8 million years ago, from the Cenomanian to the Turonian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Turonian (100.5 to 89.8 million years ago)
